claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child, Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16, I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in full-time education or registered with a careers service, or has Alex left education/training?**

This is important because Child Benefit eligibility can continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex actually left school recently, but they've just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's helpful information.

To clarify further: **Is Alex registered with a careers service or a similar government-approved body (such as Connexions in England)?** This registration would need to be because Alex is not currently in employment or full-time education and is looking for work or training opportunities.

Also, **how long ago did Alex leave school, and when did they register with the careers service?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex registered with the careers service - it's the local Connexions service here in England. They left school just a few weeks ago, and signed up with Connexions shortly after that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. It's good that Alex registered with Connexions shortly after leaving school.

I have a couple more questions to complete the eligibility assessment:

1. **Are you responsible for Alex** – meaning Alex lives with you and you're responsible for their day-to-day care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me and I'm responsible for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions:

**Do you live in the UK?** And also, **is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. And no, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex has recently left school
- Alex has registered with Connexions (a government-sponsored careers service) shortly after leaving school
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you and you are responsible for them
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex (age 16):**
- Although Alex has left school, the rules allow Child Benefit to continue for **up to 20 weeks** when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service.
- Since Alex has registered with Connexions (which qualifies as a government-sponsored careers service), you meet this requirement.
- You also meet all the other criteria: you live in the UK, Alex lives with you, you're responsible for their care, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

**Important things to note:**
- This eligibility extension lasts for **up to 20 weeks** from when Alex left education/registered with the careers service.
- If Alex starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week, starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit in their own right, your Child Benefit for them would stop.
- If Alex returns to approved full-time education or training before the 20 weeks ends, your eligibility could continue until they are up to 20 years old.

I hope this helps! Is there anything else you'd like to know?
